mainEntity.name: What should I do if AI keeps inventing facts in my social media posts?

acceptedAnswer.text:
If AI-generated content has been inaccurate, stop the workflow, identify the failure pattern, correct the source instructions, and review any already-published material. Do not simply ask the same system to “be more accurate” without changing its inputs or controls.

Context: Run My AI Biz’s process emphasizes source verification, human checkpoints, and restrictions against invented statistics, proof, or income claims. Those controls can be written directly into a social-content prompt and checklist.

Key factors:
- Identify whether the error came from the source, prompt, model, or editor.
- Add required citations or source fields internally.
- Flag uncertain statements instead of filling gaps.
- Correct public errors promptly and transparently.

Practical guidance: Build a failure log showing the original output, error, corrected version, and prevention rule. Run a small test batch before restoring regular scheduling.

A documented correction loop is more reliable than trusting a polished draft.
acceptedAnswer.description: Pause publishing, audit recent posts, identify the source of the error, and add source fields, uncertainty flags, and mandatory human review. Correct published mistakes promptly, document the failure, and test a small batch before resuming the workflow.
